prerequisites: Theoretical knowledge in the field of differential and integral calculus with one variable.
Ability to solve applied problems of differential and integral calculus with one variable (to be acquired in module Mathematics 1).

learning_outcomes.text: Master mathematical methods for dealing with problems in almost all areas of mechanical engineering.
Possess fundamental and advanced knowledge of mathematics to adequately handle problems in most subsequent modules.
Possess knowledge of the theory of the topics mentioned below in mathematics, insofar as they are relevant for application-oriented use in engineering.
Possess knowledge of mathematical methods for the topics mentioned below to solve problems specifically for engineering questions.
Gain practical experience in the application-oriented use of what has been learned to concrete problems.
Apply mathematical methods to address problems in numerous areas of mechanical engineering.
Explain fundamental and advanced mathematical concepts.
Apply mathematical methods of the topics mentioned below specifically to solve engineering problems.
Apply structures and procedures of Linear Algebra.
Apply multivariable differential calculus in engineering contexts.
Calculate multivariable integrals for technical problems.
Explain connections of vector analysis with line and surface integrals.
Solve ordinary differential equations in engineering applications.
Determine advanced mathematical tools for engineering sciences based on case studies in individual, partner, and group work.
Implement improvements to calculations under guidance and through peer feedback, and critically discuss them.

syllabus_topics: Vector analysis of line and surface integrals
teaching_methods: Lecture on theoretical foundations and basic instruments of the content, illustrated with engineering examples

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with calculation examples and theory questions
